primitives.name: Action Item State Transition
primitives.verbatim_quote: Status Due Date Done Notes Prepare weekly team meeting agenda Alice High In Progress 2025-12-17 00:00:00
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_i': 'Action item identifier (dimensionless)', 'P_i': 'Priority level {Low, Medium, High} (ordinal)', 'S_i': 'Status {Not Started, In Progress, Pending Review, Completed} (ordinal)', 'D_i': 'Due date (ISO 8601 datetime)', 'T_i': 'Time elapsed since assignment (days)'}
primitives.assumptions: State transitions follow Markovian dynamics; priority influences transition rate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Transition probability becomes deterministic at D_i ≤ current date.

layer2.mapping: Each action item maps to a node in a directed acyclic graph where edges represent valid state transitions weighted by priority.
layer2.telemetry: Completion rate per priority tier over time window.

primitives.name: Priority Weighted Task Queue
primitives.verbatim_quote: last week's minutes Update project timeline Bob Medium Not Started 2025-12-20 00:00:00 False Align with new
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q': 'Task queue (set of action items)', 'w_i': 'Weight assigned to item i based on P_i (real scalar)', 'r_i': 'Rate of progress for item i (items/day)'}
primitives.assumptions: Higher priority items receive higher weight; queue order determined by weighted rank.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Queue becomes saturated when r_i < threshold for all i ∈ Q.

layer2.mapping: Queue kernel derived from weighted sum of priority vectors across all active tasks.
layer2.telemetry: Average wait time before execution per priority class.

primitives.name: Temporal Resource Allocation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Not Started 2025-12-22 00:00:00 False Use brand colors Schedule client feedback session Frank High Completed 2025-12-15
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_t': 'Resource pool available at time t (hours)', 't_d': 'Duration required for task d (hours)', 't_s': 'Start time of task s (datetime)', 't_e': 'End time of task e (datetime)'}
primitives.assumptions: Resources are non-renewable; allocation respects precedence constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Allocation fails if ∑t_d > R_t for any t.

layer2.mapping: Allocation problem is isomorphic to a bin packing optimization over temporal intervals.
layer2.telemetry: Utilization ratio of resources over time horizon.

The state transition model assumes Markovian behavior, allowing probabilistic forecasting via Bayesian inference. Dualities emerge between priority levels and task urgency, with high-priority items exhibiting faster convergence to completion. Failure modes include deadlock (no progress), saturation (queue overflow), and misalignment (resource mismatch). These primitives enable GSI to compute expected completion times and GSE to simulate optimal scheduling policies.
